findings.highlight: she’s filled with nothing but disgust and loathing
findings.evidenceJa: 顔を背け、体をねじる少女の反応
findings.governingReading: Sakura turns her face away and twists her body in physical revulsion and resistance.
findings.explanation: The English omits both defensive bodily actions.

findings.governingReading: Sakura’s reaction contains only revulsion and resistance.
findings.explanation: The English replaces resistance with a second word for disgust, erasing her active refusal.

findings.governingReading: Shinji slightly lowers a hand he had started to extend.
findings.explanation: The English turns an incipient movement into a fully outstretched hand.

findings.governingReading: Sakura is backing away from Shinji.
findings.explanation: The English replaces retreat and resistance with static proximity.

findings.highlight: She has cursed for a long time
findings.evidenceJa: ずっと前から恨んでいたんだ
findings.governingReading: Sakura realizes she has resented this world since long ago.
findings.explanation: The English changes sustained resentment into an unspecified act of cursing.

findings.evidenceJa: 楽しいんじゃなくて、楽しかった……？
findings.governingReading: Sakura catches herself saying it “was fun” rather than “is fun,” and that tense contrast triggers recognition of earlier killings.
findings.explanation: The English repeats only the past form and erases the load-bearing contrast.

findings.governingReading: Her inquiry proceeds: when, where, what.
findings.explanation: The English swaps the first two questions.

findings.evidenceJa: わたしは夢なんか見ていない
findings.governingReading: Sakura realizes in first person that she has not been seeing dreams at all.
findings.explanation: The English shifts her inward first person into external third-person narration.

findings.evidenceJa: 夜な夜な街を徘徊して
findings.governingReading: Sakura roamed the town night after night.
findings.explanation: The English changes repeated nights into movement during one night.

findings.highlight: more tears flow out the more she laughs
findings.evidenceJa: 笑えば笑うほどボロボロと崩れていって
findings.governingReading: The more Sakura laughs, the more she crumbles to pieces, while her tears will not stop.
findings.explanation: The English replaces her accelerating collapse with increased tears.
The English changes inability to stop crying into comparative quantity.

findings.governingReading: Shinji is no longer moving because he is dead.
findings.explanation: The English says only that he is silent, weakening the physical finality.

findings.highlight: Someone was there, trying hard not to turn her into it
findings.governingReading: Sakura had desperately restrained herself so she would not become that.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the restraint to someone else and changes self-control into preventing an external transformation.

findings.highlight: There was never any hope for her
findings.evidenceJa: そんなもの、初めから全部無駄だった
findings.governingReading: In despair, Sakura concludes that all those efforts had been futile from the beginning.
findings.explanation: The English turns her judgment about efforts into an absolute narrator-like claim that Sakura herself never had hope.

findings.highlight: She doesn’t even need to acknowledge such a question
findings.evidenceJa: そんな事は、もう頷くまでもない
findings.governingReading: Zouken’s accusation is a statement so obvious to Sakura that it no longer warrants even a nod.

findings.highlight: Foremost in her mind is the relative
findings.evidenceJa: 何度も何度も現れたのは、遠坂凛
findings.governingReading: Rin appears again and again among Sakura’s imagined victims.
findings.explanation: The English changes recurrence into prominence.
